title: Timeline of the Lee Resolution and Independence Efforts
learningObjectives: Sequence the Continental Congress's move toward independence from its 1775 meeting through 1777
Identify the three parts of the Lee Resolution
Order the New York vote and the delayed treaty and confederation plans

explanations.text: The Continental Congress became the governing body of the colonies during the Revolution, with its second meeting gathering in Philadelphia in 1775.

evidence.quote: The colonists elected delegates to attend a Continental Congress that eventually became the governing body of the union during the Revolution.
Its second meeting convened in Philadelphia in 1775.

explanations.text: The Lee Resolution proposed three actions: declaring independence, seeking foreign alliances, and creating a plan for confederation.

evidence.quote: The Lee Resolution contained three parts: a declaration of independence, a call to form foreign alliances, and "a plan for confederation."

explanations.text: After the resolution, later steps included New York's July 1776 vote and longer delays for treaty and confederation plans into 1777.

evidence.quote: New York cast no vote until the newly elected New York Convention upheld the Declaration of Independence on July 9, 1776.
The plan for making treaties was not approved until September of 1776; the plan of confederation was delayed until November of 1777.
